stage_a.note: Jason delivers the rhyming story with a smile and upbeat, festive tone throughout.
Jason and Cooper actively perform the pitch with theatrical energy and clear excitement.
Jason greets the panel warmly with a smile and maintains a very friendly demeanor.

venture.description: Clip-on ornaments and lights for decorating facial hair.
venture.note: A fun holiday accessory for men with beards.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason introduces himself, Cooper, and Santa, asking for 150k for 10 percent of his company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason tells a story about Santa growing bored of his usual outfit and trying ugly sweaters.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Cooper suggests putting stuff in Santa's beard.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason explains Santa clipped bright ornaments into his beard, showing holiday spirit.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Santa excitedly names the product Beardaments.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason says they can be clipped anywhere, even chest hair, but Santa wanted more ways to decorate.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Cooper says the elves made beard oil, glitter, and lights.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason explains the lights allow seeing through the night, making Santa look great.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Cooper asks the sharks to make his Christmas wish come true.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason asks the sharks to watch their money grow.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason says they will pass out some samples to the sharks.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara remarks that she thought she had seen it all.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara says she cannot wait to put the ornaments on and asks Lori.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason asks Lori what she thinks of the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert teases that the beard is not his best look.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Cooper tells the sharks they can clip the ornaments anywhere.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin thanks Cooper for the suggestion.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert says he thinks the ornaments will look terrific.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason announces that Santa and the elf have to go wrap presents and sends them off.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Jason why he came up with this idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason explains he started it for a Christmas party, sold out online, and made 80k the first year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what the sales were in the second year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason states that the second year brought in 155,000 in sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what the sales were last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason says last year they did 462,000 in sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks what the sales are year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason replies they are projecting to do about 600 to 700 thousand in sales this year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if all the sales are direct to customer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason confirms that all sales are direct to customer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark expresses disbelief at the impressive sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason volunteers that regular ornaments sell for 9.99 and cost 1.66 to make.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks what he charges for the light-up ornaments.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason answers they sell for 19.99 and cost 4.26 to make.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how many ornaments come in a pack.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason clarifies there are 10 regular ornaments and 6 lights in a pack.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how long the lights last.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason explains they last about two days of continuous use and can be turned off.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if he wants them to burn out so customers buy again, asking where the switch is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason points out the location of the on and off switch.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert questions how many people actually save a ten-dollar item.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how Jason is acquiring customers from the specific subset of men with facial hair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason explains that viral videos with 130 million views brought in customers with zero marketing cost.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks if Jason can repeat that viral success every year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason says he maintained sales last year by doing a ton of email blasts to existing customers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Jason what his professional background is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason states he is a director of sales for a telecom distributor.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks to confirm that he is not an e-commerce expert.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason confirms he is bootstrapping the business and shipping products from his basement.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark compliments Jason, saying he is killing it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason mentions he has ideas for where he wants to take the business next.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what those ideas are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason suggests sports licensing to sell ornaments with team logos at stadiums.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert expresses doubt that sports licensing is a great idea.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what Jason wants the 150,000 dollars for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason lists licensing, expanding to other holidays, getting into retail, and international expansion as his goals.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark praises the business but says he does not see it as investable for himself, and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori agrees it is a fun idea but says he does not need a shark, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason states he is not there just for the money, but wants help growing to 5 million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks why the company is worth a 1.5 million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason explains he expects 250 to 300 thousand in net profit this year, justifying a 5x multiple.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara says trying to create new markets for a single product is a mistake and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason thanks Barbara for her feedback.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert says it is a part-time gig and he wants an entrepreneur who is all in, exiting.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how he would get his 150,000 dollar investment back.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason says Kevin would get his money back through distributions as they grow the business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin notes he is the only shark who has made money selling crazy chicken things.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert jokes that he wants to draw a cat for Jason.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason acknowledges the joke, admitting it was silly.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin compares it to his successful Potato Parcel deal, noting his own lack of hair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason takes off his hat to reveal his bald head in solidarity with Kevin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark reacts with surprise and amusement to Jason's bald head.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin talks to himself, asking what his gut says about the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin says the deal is great but too frivolous, and decides to pass.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert jokes that a frivolous deal is exactly Kevin's style.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason tells Kevin he likes money just as much and they can make it work.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin offers 150,000 dollars for a 25 percent stake in the company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert jokingly says deal on Jason's behalf.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jason accepts Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin expresses his own surprise at making the deal.

exchanges.label: growth ideas and use of funds

decisions.note: Not investable for me, you don't need us.
Fun kitschy idea but you don't need a shark.
Trying to create new markets for a single product is a mistake.
Part-time gig, want an entrepreneur who is all in.
Re-enters the deal and offers 150k for 25%.

record.notes: Kevin explicitly passes at 7:42, but Jason pushes back and Kevin makes an offer at 8:00, re-entering the deal.
